storm.summary_layperson: Mostly quiet through the evening — NWS gives a slight chance of showers after 5 PM with a better chance of showers and isolated thunderstorms developing late tonight into early Monday, but nothing is on radar approaching the cove right now.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer working tonight — Sound water (75.6°F) and air (75.2°F) are essentially the same temperature, so there's no stabilizing effect in play, though there's also nothing incoming to need it right now.
storm.detail_html:
Nothing is on KOKX radar approaching the cove right now — no storm cells, no active NWS alerts. CAPE is negligible at 20 J/kg, so there's no fuel for storms to develop locally at this hour.

The Sound offers no protective marine layer tonight: water (75.6°F) and air (75.2°F) are within half a degree of each other, so the mechanism that normally chokes incoming storms as they cross the Sound isn't available — but there's also nothing incoming to choke.

NWS's afternoon discussion (OKX, issued 3:31 PM) flags a slight chance of showers after 5 PM, building toward better shower/isolated-thunderstorm chances late tonight into Monday morning as a warm front and low pressure track through — but explicitly calls out limited instability and says severe thunderstorms are not expected through the event.

Most likely outcome for the window: quiet through 10 PM, with the better chance of showers arriving after the window closes, overnight into Monday morning. The cove isn't seeing anything different from surrounding towns tonight — this is a regional quiet stretch, not a local deflection story.

What would change the call: CAPE building above 1500 J/kg, cells appearing on KOKX within 50 mi, or an NWS watch/advisory going up. None of those are true as of this run.

Data caveat: Buoy 44040 (WLIS) is offline (UConn ERDDAP 404), so the over-water read is missing; the cove reading relies on Bridgeport Harbor (BRHC3) instead.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient wind — no sea breeze in play

hourly.shift_note: holding after sunset — gradient day, no thermal collapse

wind.tactics_blurb: Steady south gradient wind, 8-11 kt through the window with no sea breeze in play — clean flow straight up the cove axis, fairly even pressure across the course. Start mid-line, sail the numbers rather than a favored side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Today is a moderate gradient-wind day — the sea breeze isn't in play. The air–water differential is essentially flat (inland air 75.2°F vs. Sound water 75.6°F, a -0.4°F gap versus the 5°F needed to build a thermal), so the south wind on the course is straight synoptic flow, not a local sea breeze.

Gradient strength: ensemble mean at authoritative stations is 10.2 kt, matching RYC's own 10-min average of 10.5 kt out of the S (182°). Direction agreement across the ensemble is 0.78 — a solid, coherent S flow from New Haven to the LI north shore, not a patchwork.

Because this is a gradient day, not a sea-breeze day, the sea-breeze direction maturation correction doesn't apply — HRRR's raw direction (178°) is a fine read on its own; no veer correction needed.

Cove geography: due-S flow is the cleanest direction the cove sees — straight up the axis, steadiest pressure of any wind angle here. Expect fairly uniform pressure across the course, so no strong left/right favor tonight.

Because this is gradient wind, not thermal, it doesn't die at sunset (7:51 PM). HRRR's model data only extends to 7:00 PM tonight; the 8–10 PM figures are extrapolated from the established gradient pattern, with the typical 1–2 kt softening moderate-gradient days show after dark as the boundary layer stabilizes.

Backdoor cold front check: KPVD (SSE, 10 kt) and KGON (S, 9 kt) are both still southerly, not NE — no backdoor threat working into the western Sound tonight; KBOS has no usable read.

data_caveats: Buoy 44040 (WLIS) offline — UConn ERDDAP fetch failing (404).

HRRR hourly forecast only extended through 7:00 PM local (f01–f04); the 8:00–10:00 PM wind figures in this window are extrapolated from the gradient-wind persistence pattern per the cove-wind-greenwich framework, not fresh model output.
